lines: Accurſe au
dit §. eiuſdem[?]

uncertain.note: spaced capitals, closed up per §3 with spaced_caps true. The numeral is set X X V I  I with a noticeably wider gap between the fourth and fifth sorts than between the others (body-4.jpg, checked at 4x and 10x); all five sorts are clear (two X, one V, two I) and the terminal point follows the last I, so the numeral is XXVII (= annotation 27), not 'XXVI I.'. The wide gap is compositor spacing only.

HARD / ESCALATE. After 'Accurſe' the line ends in an over-inked cluster. Measured on the raw scan (raw/img069.jpg, y 3266-3292 = x-height band): three ink runs, x 2238-2262 (w 24), x 2268-2280 (w 12), x 2282-2298 (w 16), the last carrying a thin faded stroke rising 11 px above x-height at columns 2290-2292 (full ascenders on this line, the key 'b' and the 'ſ' of Accurſe, rise 21 px). Reference widths on the note's second line: d = 27, i = 13, t = 14, u = 27. Read as 'au' (the 30 px span 2268-2298 matching the 27 px 'u' of 'Accurſe', the faint raised stroke taken as a speck or the tip of a broken sort), which gives 'Accurſe au | dit §. eiuſdem', i.e. 'audit §. eiuſdem', referring back to the '§. eiuſdem' of note a. The competing readings are 'aud' (the third run a d with a faded ascender, which would double the d of line 2) and 'ait' (a + dotted i + t), neither of which yields sense. Reader B may well read 'aud'; a human should confirm at the original.

the mark after 'eiuſdem' cannot be identified. Measured on the raw scan: x 2282-2297 (w 15), top y 3334 (= x-height, 3331), bottom y 3362 (6 px below the baseline, 3356); the clean period after '§' on the same line is w 8 and sits y 3350-3357. So the mark is letter-sized and descends: too tall and wide for a period, and it rises to x-height, unlike a comma. Possibly a comma with ink spread, a broken sort, or the 3-shaped ꝫ. Transcribed [?]. The three sorts before it are 'd i t' (d with a full ascender and bowl, i with its dot, t with crossbar) at 10-20x, so the line begins 'dit', not 'ict'.

the sort between 'iij.' and 'eiuſ-' is the same over-inked paragraph sign read as § on p045 (a small loop opening left at the top, a straight top bar, bowls to the right and a tail below the foot); transcribed § for consistency with transcription/final/p045.json margin_notes[0]. The numeral is 'i' plus the italic ij-sort (one dot over the first stem, two dots over the second, which descends), i.e. iij, checked at 20x.

'dem.' has a badly over-inked m (a solid blob at reading size; three humps resolve at 12x). The title is abbreviated very short, 'de te.' (t with crossbar then e, at 20x) — presumably D. de teſtibus, which suits the annotation's subject. A faint speck sits above the final point, so the mark could be a colon rather than a period; the lower dot is round, on the baseline and much darker, and is read as a period.

the first sort is heavily inked; read as c (canon-law 'c.' = capitulum, as in 'c. ex tranſmiſſa' on p045), giving the decretal incipit 'c. in noſtra' under the same title. It could be read as ſ. The line-end hyphen after 'il' is clear.

two very faint specks sit in the space between 'lo' and 'titul' (checked at 22x); they are much lighter and more irregular than the printed points elsewhere in the note and are read as dirt, not as a point. If they are a point the line would read 'lo. titul.'

uncertain.note: double-s check at 12x: 'neceſſaires' is set with two tall long s (ſſ ligature), not ſs. Same check made on 'aſſeuroient' (blocks[1].lines[11], ſſ) and on 'inſuffiſans' (blocks[3].lines[17], which is ſ + ff + i + ſ, no double s).

uncertain.note: sic: 'ſen' printed with long s and no apostrophe (= ſ'en); no apostrophe present at 10x. Transcribed as printed per §1.

uncertain.note: the word-break sign after 'va' is a short thick stroke set near mid height, easily mistaken for a point (body-7.jpg, checked at 10x); transcribed as a single '-' per §1, the word continuing 'lable' on the next line. The preceding line ends 'l'ad' with no break sign at all, which is normal for this print.

uncertain.note: last line of the page; the paragraph runs on to p050, so continues_next is true. The final r is the tailed line-end r of this fount, transcribed as an ordinary r. 'font' has a true f (full crossbar), not long s. The print sets 'lable:car', 'deux,de' and 'de ſoy' tight; normalized per §1.

the print sets a justification space before the final point ('grandes . Le') and before the comma ('raiſons , &'); normalized away per §1. The mark after 'grandes' is a round dot on the baseline (period), checked at 4x against the commas on the same line.

uncertain.text: cauſe, pour le conflict des coniectures &
uncertain.note: 'conflict' is set with the fl and ct ligatures and is decomposed per §2; the c of 'ct' is clear at 10x, so the word is conflict, not conflit. 'coniectures' and 'contradiction' likewise carry the ct ligature.

uncertain.text: premiere, vn grãd nombre de teſmoins,
uncertain.note: the mark over the a of 'grãd' is a tilde (flat bar for the omitted n), clear at 6x; not expanded per §2. 'premiere' is printed without an accent (sic).

the only thing in the foot block is a plain roman capital D, with no numeral and no point, set below the last line and right of centre (foot.jpg, 10x). Read as the gathering signature: the corpus shows gatherings of 16 leaves signed on the first four rectos (A on f.1, A ij on f.3 … B on f.17, C on f.33), so f.49 is D. There are no foot citations and no catchword.
spaced roman capitals, closed up per §3 and §5; printed TOLOSE (not THOLOSE) on this recto, kept as printed. The folio 49 stands at the outer right of the head line.
